value: 256 Hz tuning fork held toward the web: escape in 58% of responses and attack in 36% (two years combined)
method: field behavioural assay on orb webs: a struck tuning fork (256 Hz or 440 Hz) brought slowly toward the web, and a metal wire touched to the abdomen; behaviour scored as escape or attack; frequency distributions compared with Fisher's exact tests
conditions: Wild spiders in their webs at accessible sites in Southeast Wales, 8 Aug to 6 Sep 2020 and 1 to 17 Aug 2021; adult females, assumed to be M. segmentata, 4 to 9 mm long; 38 of 50 spiders analysed in 2020 and 40 of 46 in 2021 (spiders removed for insufficient data, mainly not returning between stimuli). No no-stimulus control: the wire was the comparison stimulus. Order was fixed in 2020 (256 Hz, 440 Hz, wire) and randomised in 2021 (random number generator); the paper reports the wire gave less consistent responses by order. 440 Hz forks provoked attacks in about 90% of responses (both years combined); highest no-response rate 16% (wire, 2020). Acoustic frequency is the stimulus label; no vibration amplitude or sound level is given in the passage read.

value: more active after exposure to waterborne chemical cues from its catfish prey; the prey (catfish) did not avoid chemical cues from the snakes
method: captive activity trials: 10 L of water from a tank holding nine striped eel catfish (Plotosus lineatus) or from an empty tank poured into one corner of the snakes' tank; activity scored as head crossings of cords in the 2 min after addition
conditions: Four wild-caught snakes (SVL 53 to 130 cm; sex not reported) from Baie des Citrons and Anse Vata, New Caledonia, January to March 2020, held 6 to 19 days in a seawater tank; stimulus order (catfish water versus control) randomised, trials 15 to 30 min apart, daytime. Snakes were about twice as active with catfish water (F1,4 = 53.57, p < 0.006, linear mixed model). Conditioning time of the catfish water and fasting state of the snakes are not stated. Catfish shelter-choice trials (nine fish, 15 replicates, 7 control versus 8 snake-scented choices, chi-square 0.06, p = 0.79) showed no avoidance; the authors note pseudoreplication. The snake response is activity, not a measured detection threshold or an identified receptor route.

method: electroantennogram of female antennae to four maize volatiles (hexanal, trans-2-hexen-1-ol, linalool, beta-caryophyllene) at 0.1, 1, 10 and 100 mg/mL in mineral oil; mineral oil blank and 100 mg/mL cis-3-hexen-1-ol positive control
conditions: Insects from eggs supplied by the National Plant Protection Scientific Observation and Experiment Station, Langfang, reared on artificial diet; n = 5 female antennae per substance, 45 s between stimuli; compound order, female age and mating status are not stated in the Methods. value: adult males were attracted to volatiles of honeydew excreted by adult males (74% response rate); females were not
method: Y-plate two-choice olfactometer: honeydew on filter paper (5 mm x 10 mm) in one arm against clean hexane-cleaned filter paper in the other; non-choosers within 3 min counted as non-responders; G-test
conditions: Adults captured weekly from the field (Ailanthus altissima, Lehigh County, Pennsylvania) and shipped overnight, 19 August to 27 September 2019, covering early (emergence), mid (mating) and late (oviposition) season; fed cut A. altissima branches, no starvation described. Honeydew was collected from males or females on A. altissima in the field. Males tested with male honeydew: G = 13.72, df = 1, alpha = 0.001, n = 35, overall response rate 74%; the paper gives no n or G for females, only that they were not attracted. Sexes were tested in alternating order, five control insects without stimulus per session checked olfactometer bias, and randomisation of arm position is not described. Honeydew from females did not significantly attract either sex (positive trend only). Synthetic compounds were tested separately and are not logged here.

value: males were significantly attracted to female-conditioned water in the mating period (chi-square 4.12, P = 0.04) but not in the non-mating period (chi-square 0.31, P = 0.58)
method: Y-maze with crude female-conditioned water in one arm against ultrapure water in the other; one test per animal, 5 min window; chi-square test
conditions: Males bought in Guilin, Guangxi, China in August 2020 (mean weight 16.22 +/- 1.82 g) and held without contact with females or pheromones; non-mating-period (NMP) males fed until January 2021 at water temperature below 15 C and mating-period (MP) males until April 2021 at above 22 C, so the two groups were tested months apart at different temperatures; 50 males per period. Conditioned water from 20 mature females fasted 48 h in 1 L ultrapure water, centrifuged 20 min (8000 rpm, 4 C). Arm positions swapped after every five animals; animals making no choice in 5 min were counted as unresponsive and excluded, and their number is not reported, nor are the arm counts in the text. The conditioned water is a crude mixture, not a single compound.
